extracted.intended_audience: administrative analysts, public administrators, government managers, and organizational study practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for analyzing an organization's functions, units, workload, and administrative sequences to improve efficiency and reconfigure organization/flows. Intended to direct onsite observation, measurement, and reclassification work by administrative analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification must be systematic and reflect true framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A classification intended for general management use must be systematic and reflect the true framework of functions; the classifier should consult extensively with officials in charge of each function, similar officials in other organizations, and knowledgeable outsiders, and the classification should be sanctioned by the top administrator so it may be accepted as a basis for planning and action by everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult widely (internal and external), ensure top-level sanction, and treat the classification as a working basis for planning and action rather than an abstract exercise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on titles or following organization structure in classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The classification should not be too greatly influenced by the titles of functions or operations (e.g., 'administrative audit,' 'review') because such words may mean anything or nothing; nor should classification necessarily follow the organization structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probe behind titles to find the real function; adapt budgetary and file classifications before using them for administrative analysis; ensure the classification shows relationships (e.g., between line and staff) rather than crystallizing existing arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function analysis — Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the direct activity (purpose of administration)? How does the administrative function facilitate the accomplishment of the direct work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey a main function and then sub-functions; gather enough information to give a comprehensive picture including how the admin function supports line activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function analysis — Necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the administrative activity in question be eliminated or curtailed? How essential is it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the activity is indispensable or can be reduced/eliminated; look for duplication or non-essential tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function analysis — Co-ordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the direct operations and the administrative work consistent within themselves and with each other? Do they conflict with other functions or with the major objectives of the organization?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for conflicts between functions and alignment with organizational objectives; consider relationships among line and staff functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function analysis — Method
rubrics_metrics.description: What operations are involved in the direct work? Specifically, how are these operations supervised?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document processes and supervisory methods; distinguish theoretical procedures from actual methods used in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function analysis — Assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: What unit or units carry on the function? What are the channels of supervision? How is the work divided — by sub-function, area of operation, or both? Are two or more units which could be combined doing the same or similar work? Is any work being done twice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare assignments across units to identify overlaps, duplications, or opportunities to combine units; trace channels of supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function analysis — Work load
rubrics_metrics.description: How much working time, and of what type and grade of employees, is required? What is the unit of output? How many such units are produced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect quantitative data on time and outputs; use workload measures to determine staffing and distribution of tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function analysis — Accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the function, as carried on and administered, serve its purpose? What improvements are needed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess effectiveness of the function and identify needed improvements; use findings as factual background for planning better administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-level onsite observation and interviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: The analyst must visit each division, section, and unit under study, sit down with the chief and staff, let each describe the job as he sees it, gain confidence, and avoid expressing conclusions before digesting facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid premature conclusions; let interviewees talk freely while ensuring questioning covers the unit thoroughly; learn actual methods from workers and supervisors rather than relying only on formal procedures or job descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit analysis — Purpose (unit-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: What, briefly, is the job that is being done? What is the transition from the raw material to the finished product? What are the criteria of satisfactory accomplishment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the unit's outputs and success criteria clearly; distinguish tasks vs duties (repeated tasks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit analysis — Relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: How does the job fit into the classification of functions and the administrative sequence of which it is a part? What are the preceding and following operations and where are they done? How does the job relate to the larger objectives of the organization?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map the unit into functional classifications and sequences; trace upstream and downstream operations and physical/organizational locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit analysis — Method (unit-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the processes in doing the work? If the job is supervisory, what are the methods of observation and control?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe actual operating methods (how work is really done), not just stated procedures; document control and supervision techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit analysis — Work load (unit-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the unit of work? Are the items or 'cases' uniform or variable? How long does it take to dispose of a unit? Does the work come in evenly or pile up?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure variability, average/min/max times; identify peaks and bottlenecks; use findings to design normal workloads for positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit analysis — Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: How many people, and of what type and grade, are assigned to the work? Are they overworked or underworked? When is overtime necessary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess staffing levels and grades; relate personnel mix to workload and identify misassignments or delegation failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit analysis — Conditions of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the office arrangements and equipment suitable? Is incoming material in the proper shape? What improvements would help?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine physical layout, equipment, and incoming materials; recommend practical improvements to reduce errors and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit analysis — Channels of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Who supervises the job? Who is supervised in connection therewith? What regular operating contacts are made with other offices—directly or through intermediaries?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document supervision lines and regular contacts; use contact mapping to reveal operating relationships between units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare formal (official) organization with actual operating organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use organization charts showing divisions and sections both in their formal power relationships (lines of authority) and in their actual operations; note discrepancies between formal statements and observed practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat organization charts as working diagrams to be changed as need arises; create an 'operating organization chart' based on observation, and revisit classifications when quantitative analysis suggests revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure executive work load using time-study methods and running records
rubrics_metrics.description: For executive work, require executives during a test period to enter a running record of activities on a daily report card showing time consumed, physical process (writing, telephoning), person contacted, and subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulate by minutes (not just number of items) and categorize (telephone calls, conferences, reading, reading & signing, writing/dictating); analyze average/maximum/minimum times and distribution to identify delegation opportunities and equitable task distribution. Use sample form (Figure 4) and consider graphical displays (lines on org chart proportional to minutes) to show operating relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept and measure variability and non-uniformity in executive tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement of executive work must not try to force uniform units but must accept differences in bulk and importance as a basic condition and even assay the non-uniformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid Procrustean unit systems; measure by time and analyze variability (averages, extremes) to inform delegation and staffing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use quantitative communication mapping to reallocate units
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabulate time spent contacting other officials and show it graphically (lines of thickness proportional to minutes) superimposed on the organization chart to reveal operating relationships and candidates for transfer or consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce inter-office traffic where possible; reallocate units so closely related activities are together; keep continuous processes within the same offices to minimize complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define tasks and administrative sequences; minimize moves
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide any sequence into steps or individual tasks, count the number of 'moves' (transfers of work/paper) required, and recognize that administrative motion takes time; the number and distance (physical and organizational) of moves should be kept as low as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the chain of transfers in a sequence and redesign flows to reduce moves; apply time-and-motion principles to transfers and communication rather than to cognitive tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator's role — focus and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrator should be responsible for dividing up work, assigning areas of operation, and regulating order and flow, but should delegate the detailed analysis and technical work of defining functions, developing assignments, and setting routines to administrative analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators should concentrate on broad policies and results while relying on analysts for voluminous technical analysis; avoid administrators getting bogged down in routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for uneven quality of duties and failure to delegate
rubrics_metrics.description: When duties assigned to an individual or group cover a wide range in required skill and importance, workers may face tasks too advanced for them or waste time on tasks below their ability — often a result of failure to delegate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify uneven duty mixes and redesign or delegate to right-grade staff; consider reassigning tasks to match skill levels and to avoid misuse of higher-grade personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise functional classification based on quantitative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis by units of organization, especially with quantitative methods, may lead to revision of the earlier qualitative classification of functions; classifications should be revised as observation accumulates new knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow functional classification to be corrected by empirical findings; let analysis by function and by unit react upon each other.
